subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — next steps
messages:
From: Sandeep Mehra <sandeep@acmeai.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@acmeai.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T16:15:00-07:00
Subject: TTFT & streaming requirements (post-demo)

Thanks again for the demo today — appreciate the walkthrough of Dedicated and the streaming options. A quick recap of what we need so the infra team can validate:

- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) target: ideally <= 200ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens).
- Streaming response behavior: we'll use SSE for the browser client and WebSocket for some server-side consumers. Chunk cadence needs to be consistent — our UX shows issues when the first chunk comes after 300ms.
- Throughput: baseline 80 QPS for text-gen, with peaks up to 120 QPS.
- Concurrency: up to 500 concurrent streaming sessions initially; possibility to burst to ~800 during campaigns.
- Payloads: median response size ~150 tokens; some long-form up to 2k tokens (less common).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can guarantee TTFT under those conditions, and what data you need from us for a realistic perf run? Attached is a lightweight profile of our request mix (acme-ttft-profile.json).

— Sandeep
Head of Product, Acme AI

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Sandeep Mehra <sandeep@acmeai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-11T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming requirements (post-demo) — next steps and bench plan

Sandeep — thanks for the clear requirements and the profile. Short version: yes, we can meet sub-200ms TTFT for short prompts in a streaming setup, but we need to validate against your exact mix (concurrency patterns + chunk cadence).

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood runs an internal perf pass using your profile + our representative models (open quantized variant we recommend). We'll measure: TTFT (cold & warm), first-chunk latency, steady-state per-token latency, and chunk cadence variance.
2) Joint benchmark with your team (we provide a script, you run in your environment or we run against a Dedicated test pool).
3) If needed, we iterate on batching/kv-cache policies and recommend config (concurrency per-worker, max-batch size, pipeline settings).

Questions / clarifications we need from you to scope the run:
- Are your short prompts always <= 128 tokens? (the TTFT target assumes this distribution).
- For SSE clients, do you require a minimum first-chunk size (e.g., 1 token vs 8–16 token prebuffer) to reduce chunk overhead?
- Do you care about absolute end-to-end time (from browser input to first visual token) vs server-side TTFT? We usually report both.

Initial numbers we expect on Redwood Dedicated (for the profile you sent):
- TTFT (server-side first token): median ~120–180ms (short prompts), P95 < 250ms depending on concurrency.
- First chunk cadence: first chunk typically within TTFT, subsequent chunks every ~120–250ms depending on model generation time and chunk size.
- Throughput/concurrency: a single 80GB A10/GPU pool node can sustain ~60–80 concurrent streaming sessions for low-latency TTFT; we can scale horizontally and use smart routing to hit your 500–800 concurrent needs.

I'll loop in Marissa (SRE/Bench lead) and Laura (Solutions) to coordinate the test plan. We'll produce a concise SLA proposal after the joint run.

Next meeting: propose Tue 4/13 10:00 PT to review results?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Singh <priya@acmeai.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Sandeep Mehra <sandeep@acmeai.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-11T14:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming requirements (post-demo)

Thanks Aditya — this looks good. Quick answers:
- Yes, short prompts are ~90% <= 128 tokens; we have a 10% long-tail.
- For browser UX we prefer the first chunk to be at least 8 tokens to avoid jittered rendering. If Redwood can do a small early chunk (8–16 tokens) within TTFT target, that would be ideal.
- We care about end-to-end perceived TTFT (browser-visible first token). We can instrument client-side but would like Redwood's server-side TTFT numbers too.

We can make an engineer available for the joint bench on Tue 4/13. Attached is a small sample payload set (included in acme-ttft-profile.json).

— Priya
Senior Engineering Manager, Acme AI

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Sandeep Mehra <sandeep@acmeai.com>, Priya Singh <priya@acmeai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming requirements (post-demo) — bench plan + ask list

Great — thanks for confirming. Confirming the plan for Tue 4/13 10:00 PT (we'll send a calendar invite). Action items before the run:
- Acme: provide a short sample of client-side instrumentation (or grant access) so we can measure perceived TTFT. If not possible, we'll run a parallel client harness.
- Acme: confirm whether SSE fallback to WebSocket is acceptable for some clients (helps us optimize connections).
- Redwood: we'll share the bench script, expected resource footprint, and a prefilled config for your profile by EOD today. Expect the following deliverables after the run:
  - Per-request CSV with server TTFT, first-chunk time, per-chunk timestamps, token counts.
  - Aggregated report (median, p90, p95, p99) and a recommendation sheet (batching, concurrency per-worker, recommended node counts).
  - Draft SLA language for TTFT and streaming reliability tied to config/committed capacity.

Attachments: redwood-ttft-sla-proposal.pdf (contains our proposed SLO wording and measurement methods).

If we hit your targets in bench we can move to a short pilot on a Dedicated pool to validate at scale.

See you Tue — invite incoming.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
